title: Meteor shower, supermoons: SoCal stargazers are in for a month of dazzling astronomical events
excerpt: The night sky is putting on quite an astronomical show this month, and there's still more to come for Southern California stargazers.
content:
• SCIENCE

The night sky is putting on quite an astronomical show this month, and there's still more to come for Southern California stargazers.

Wednesday, November 18, 2026 10:25PM

LOS ANGELES (KABC) -- Southern California stargazers have several reasons to look up this month, with the Leonids meteor shower peaking this week and a supermoon expected next week.

Under ideal dark-sky conditions, the Leonids meteor shower could produce up to 15 meteors an hour. Tim Thompson of Mt. Wilson Observatory said people who venture outside could see Jupiter and Mars along with the meteors.

"You should have good viewing of the meteors at that time, too," Thompson said. "If you go into the dark night and wait until 2 o'clock or 3 o'clock in the morning, you can see Jupiter and Mars together and the meteors. It lines up happily."

Another celestial event is expected Nov. 24, when a supermoon will light up the night sky. A supermoon occurs when a full moon coincides with its closest approach to Earth, making it appear slightly bigger and brighter than usual.

Another supermoon is expected on Christmas Eve, Thompson said.

"We have another one the night of Christmas Eve, actually, in December," Thompson said. "This year we get them closer together, November and December."

For the best viewing conditions, stargazers should get away from city lights and give their eyes time to adjust to the darkness. Rain in the forecast, however, could interfere with the view.
